edition.sessionCovered: Tue, Oct 27 close / Wed, Oct 28 early
edition.stripNote: Wed 28 Oct. FOMC decision today 2pm ET — 93% chance of hold. Israeli election results being digested. Record Hormuz attacks in October.
edition.scoreboardCaption: Wed 28 Oct early vs Tue 27 close. Ranked best to worst.

overview: Oil steadied on Wednesday as markets awaited the Fed's rate decision at 2pm ET, with Brent edging up 0.4% to $114.40 after two sessions of declines on renewed Middle East diplomacy. WTI firmed 0.6% to $100.55. Israel's general election on Tuesday — the first since the Knesset dissolved in July — added a new political variable to the regional conflict, with results potentially reshaping war policy toward Iran. October has set a record for shipping attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, with the Washington Institute counting 28 confirmed incidents and 11 VLCCs damaged — about 3.5% of the global supertanker fleet. Newcastle coal held at $150, while Asian LNG (JKM) pulled back 1.4% to $31.74 per MMBtu. The US SPR remains at its 40-year low of 282.6 million barrels.

Gold held above $4,050 ahead of the FOMC decision, consolidating after two sessions of gains. Markets price a 93% chance the Fed holds rates at 3.75–4.00%, but a December hike is priced near 73% probability via CME FedWatch — the September minutes flagged another increase as 'likely appropriate by year end.' Copper firmed 0.2% to $6.64/lb as US-China trade tensions eased further, with Treasury Secretary Bessent confirming the threatened 100% tariff is off the table. Grains bounced modestly: corn rose 0.5% to 451¢, wheat gained 0.4% to 612¢, and soybeans ticked up to 1,231¢. Chinese lithium carbonate rebounded 1.1% to 99,350 yuan, recovering from last week's first break below the key 100,000 yuan level. Bitcoin traded near $79,700 ahead of the rate decision, with $80,000 acting as resistance.

watchItems.title: FOMC decision today, 2pm ET
watchItems.text: The Fed announces its rate decision Wednesday with markets pricing a 93% chance of holding at 3.75–4.00%. September's quarter-point hike was the first since the cycle paused earlier this year. The December meeting (8–9 Dec) is now the key event, with futures pricing roughly a 73% chance of another hike. Chair Warsh's press conference at 2:30pm will be watched for guidance on whether oil-driven inflation has eased enough to pause or if the committee sees further tightening ahead.

watchItems.title: Israeli election reshapes Middle East calculus
watchItems.text: Israel voted in its first general election since the Knesset dissolved in July, with results being digested by markets on Wednesday. The outcome could shift war policy toward Iran and the broader Hormuz conflict. Brent dipped on Tuesday as some parties advocating de-escalation performed well in early counts, but crude held above $114 on uncertainty about coalition formation and the timeline for any policy change. Markets watching whether new leadership pursues diplomacy or escalation.

watchItems.title: Hormuz attacks set monthly record in October
watchItems.text: The Washington Institute counted 28 confirmed attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz in October — the highest monthly total since tracking began in 2017. Eleven VLCCs were damaged, accounting for about 3.5% of the global fleet. UKMTO has logged 135 conflict-related incidents since February 28. Shipowners are still loading inside the Gulf, drawn by daily freight rates above $1 million and steep producer discounts against dated Brent, but the rate of fleet damage is accelerating.

watchItems.title: US-China trade thaw lifts copper and risk appetite
watchItems.text: Copper approached three-month highs after Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed the threatened 100% tariff is off the table and Beijing agreed to pause its planned rare earth export control expansion for a year. The Grasberg mine accident and El Teniente production issues in Chile added supply-side support. But gallium exports from China have not meaningfully resumed despite the Busan truce, with domestic Chinese gallium at 1,740 yuan per kilogram. Markets watching whether the diplomatic thaw translates into trade flow improvements.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold held above $4,050 on Wednesday, consolidating after two sessions of gains as traders positioned ahead of the FOMC decision due at 2pm ET. Markets price roughly a 93% chance the Fed holds rates at 3.75–4.00%, but a December hike is priced near 73%. The metal remains about 28% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver was essentially flat at $54.40 on Wednesday, tracking gold's cautious pre-FOMC consolidation. The metal remains down about 14% on the month, one of its worst monthly performances of the year. The gold-silver ratio held near 75.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent edged up 0.4% to $114.40 on Wednesday, steadying after two sessions of declines on renewed Middle East diplomacy and Israel's Knesset election on Tuesday. WTI firmed to $100.55. October set a record for Hormuz shipping attacks — the Washington Institute counted 28 confirmed incidents, with 11 VLCCs damaged. The US SPR remains at a 40-year low of 282.6 million barrels. Shipowners still load inside the Gulf, drawn by daily freight rates above $1 million.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper firmed 0.2% to $6.64 per pound on Wednesday as US-China trade tensions eased further, with Treasury Secretary Bessent confirming the threatened 100% tariff is off the table. The Grasberg mine accident in Indonesia and production issues at Codelco's El Teniente in Chile added supply-side support. Roughly flat on the month.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal ticked up 0.2% to $150.00, holding near its recent range as the Hormuz gas shock keeps Asian utilities dependent on coal. The IEA forecasts record global coal demand of 8.94 billion tonnes this year. Indonesia, the largest exporter, cut its production target with shipments running below 2025 levels.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum firmed 0.15% to $1,540 on Wednesday, finding modest support ahead of the Fed decision. The metal remains down about 11% on the month as elevated yields and a firm dollar weigh on the PGM complex. WPIC's forecast of an 18% drop in total platinum demand this year continues to cap rallies.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium edged up 0.3% to $1,032 on Wednesday, holding near multi-month lows. The metal is down about 22% on the month. Auto-driven demand continues to weaken as platinum substitution in gasoline catalysts accelerates and EV market share grows.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: ~30 transits/day vs 85 pre-war · 28 attacks in Oct
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz recorded its worst month for shipping attacks since tracking began in 2017, with the Washington Institute counting 28 confirmed incidents — including 11 VLCCs damaged, about 3.5% of the global supertanker fleet. UKMTO has logged 135 conflict-related incidents since the US-Israeli war with Iran began on February 28. Israel's general election on October 27 added a new political variable. US-facilitated transits remain above 30 per day, still far below the pre-war baseline of 85.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn firmed 0.5% to 451 cents on Wednesday, bouncing modestly ahead of the FOMC decision. The US corn harvest continues near the five-year average pace. Managed money still holds substantial short positions in corn.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: December wheat rose 0.35% to 612 cents on Wednesday, recovering slightly from Tuesday's lows. Managed money holds its largest net short position in wheat. Winter wheat planting remains on schedule and export demand is subdued.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: November soybeans ticked up 0.15% to 1,231 cents on Wednesday, stabilising after Monday's two-month low. The US harvest continues to run ahead of the five-year average, pointing to a record crop. Brazilian production estimates remain robust.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin traded near $79,700 on Wednesday morning, cautious ahead of the 2pm ET FOMC decision. The $80,000 level has flipped to resistance, with $79,300 as immediate support and $77,000 below that. BlackRock's IBIT saw $110.3 million in net inflows on Monday, but broader spot BTC ETFs remain under pressure with $773.5 million in net outflows last Thursday and Friday. Ethereum held at $2,307.

desk.name: LNG
desk.sum: Asian LNG spot (JKM) pulled back 1.4% to $31.74 per MMBtu on Wednesday, easing from near $32 after a week of gains. Hormuz disruption continues to threaten Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual export capacity. European TTF held near €97 per MWh. Henry Hub natural gas rose 2% to $3.06, though the gap with global spot markets remains wide.

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated with CFR Southeast Asia around $1,100–1,300 a tonne. Domestic Chinese sulfur trades at 5,564 yuan a tonne, down 0.9% on the day. Middle East FOB prices hold at $765 (Kuwait) and $740 (Qatar). Hormuz disruption continues squeezing sulfuric acid supply — the essential input for copper leaching, phosphate fertilizer, and oil refining.

desk.name: Potash
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds near $367.50 a tonne, little changed. China's 2025 contract settled at $348 a tonne. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions, routing through non-aligned buyers.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) held near 90,000 yuan a tonne, consolidating after the mid-October drop from its post-holiday high of 105,000 yuan. SMM expects prices to find a bottom and consolidate near current levels, with limited further panic selling as supply remains structurally tight. Demand from flame retardant and PV glass sectors is subdued.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: China exports −94% since controls · domestic Ga ¥1,740/kg
desk.sum: Gallium remains near a record $1,850 a kilogram outside China, up over 200% since early 2025. Chinese domestic gallium trades at 1,740 yuan per kilogram. Beijing's Document No. 46 export controls retain a presumption of denial for US end users, and the Busan truce's Document No. 72 suspension has not meaningfully restored exports. China produces about 98% of global gallium and 60% of germanium.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) averaged about $5.02 a pound in 2025, slipping from $5.44 in 2024 as steel demand softened. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.sum: ICE cocoa rose 1.3% to $5,563 a tonne on Wednesday, extending its recovery from recent lows. Ivory Coast arrivals remain up 19.8% in the current marketing year and ICE inventories climbed to a 2.25-year high, capping the upside. However, forecasts for a strong El Niño affecting West African producers into 2027 keep the downside limited.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.sum: Cobalt traded at $34,620 a tonne, roughly steady. The DRC (70% of global mine supply) maintains export quotas of 96,600 tonnes a year to support prices, but the EV battery chemistry shift from NMC to LFP continues to structurally reduce demand. Aerospace and superalloy uses provide a floor.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate spot rebounded 1.1% to 99,350 yuan a tonne on Wednesday, recovering from last week's first break below the key 100,000 yuan level. Futures remain near 94,000 yuan, roughly halved from the mid-May peak above 200,000 yuan. Goldman Sachs projects the global market flipping from a 404,000-tonne deficit in 2026 to a 444,000-tonne surplus by 2028.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades around $2,570 a tonne ($2.57/kg), firming on tight supply from Southeast Asia where Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia produce 70% of the world's latex. Fungal leaf blight (Pestalotiopsis) continues to reduce yields across the region. Auto-sector demand remains solid.
